input.question: Why do people think that there are an infinite number of universes?
input.ground_truth: Depends how you define universe. Theres the observable universe which is finite. We can only see so far out past earth. Most people believe space is infinite. If it wasnt, then what would exist after space? Anyway, if space is infinite and our observable universe is finite, then it is highly likely that other universes exist, and that there are an unlimited amount of them. If you define the universe as literally everything. Then there is only 1. And it is infinite. Any variations of it would just be contained in itself.

Okay! Imagine you have a big box of crayons. In that box, you have lots and lots of crayons — so many that you can never count them all, even if you try your best every day for your whole life. Some people think that the universe (the big space everything is in) is a little bit like that box of crayons, but even bigger!

So, when some grown-ups talk about "an infinite number of universes," they mean there could be so many universes — like so many boxes of crayons — that you can never, ever finish counting them. It's like saying there is no last universe; there is always another one, just like there is always another number if you keep counting up forever.

But we don't know for sure if this is true — it's just something some smart people think might be possible!
